claims.feature: other: invented world as historical ethic
claims.claim: Cabon writes that one reason Kay sets fact-based plots in invented worlds is his refusal to betray historical figures by presuming their reactions.
claims.source: Mikael Cabon, « Les Chevaux célestes pour "les cancres" », Éditions L'Atalante, 11 July 2014
claims.quote: son refus de trahir les personnages historiques en présumant de leurs réactions

claims.claim: The translator's own page for Voile vers Sarance carries the line announcing Kay's Byzantine epic in a new translation.
claims.source: Mikael Cabon, translator's own page for Voile vers Sarance (L'Atalante)
claims.page: back-cover text reproduced on the page

claims.claim: Elbakin forum readers record that A Brightness Long Ago had already been translated by Élisabeth Vonarburg and published in 2020 before the L'Atalante version appeared.
claims.source: Elbakin.net forum thread on Comme un diamant dans ma mémoire (reader posts)
claims.quote: Il avait déjà été traduit par Élisabeth Vonarburg et paru en 2020

claims.claim: Kay's site records that The Last Light of the Sun audiobook was read by Holter Graham.
claims.quote: Last Light of the Sun is wrapped, read by Holter Graham

claims.claim: Kay's site records that A Song for Arbonne was read by Euan Morton, who also sang the songs.
claims.quote: read by Euan Morton (who sang the songs, as well)

claims.claim: Gillossen calls Kay's multiplication of period terms in The Last Light of the Sun sometimes incidental to what it adds to the story.
claims.source: Gillossen, critique of Les Derniers Feux du soleil, Elbakin.net, 19 April 2009

claims.feature: other: competing memories of one event
claims.claim: Siriane observes that in Children of Earth and Sky the same events can be examined from the points of view of different characters, which she calls a kaleidoscopic effect.
claims.source: Siriane, critique of Children of Earth and Sky, Elbakin.net, 20 January 2017
claims.quote: ce qui donne un intéressant effet kaléidoscopique

claims.claim: Elbakin.net records that after a first publication at Le Pré aux Clercs the novel was reissued by L'Atalante with a translation by Mikael Cabon.
claims.source: Elbakin.net, update of 20 August 2021 appended to the Les Derniers Feux du soleil page
claims.quote: avec cette fois une traduction de Mikael Cabon

claims.claim: Haggard criticises The Summer Tree for having characters stop the action dead to make a flowery speech.
claims.source: Cynthia Sally Haggard, review of the Simon Vance audiobook of The Summer Tree, 24 May 2020
claims.quote: stops the action dead in order to make a flowery speech
